co_turtle_rocks.blurb: Turtle Rocks is a granite crag a few miles outside Buena Vista, sitting among the larger formations of the Arkansas Valley. It holds roughly eighteen routes, split between bolted lines and gear climbs, plus a single top-rope and one aid line. Grades cluster in the 5.10 range, with a handful of easier trad pitches around 5.6 to 5.9 and a few harder sport leads in the 5.11s and low 5.12s. Expect short to medium single pitches on slabby faces with big crystals, and some crack lines. Getting to a few of the lines involves scrambling, so it suits experienced climbers more than beginners or kids. A narrow shaded notch nearby offers relief from the sun.

co_continental_crag.blurb: Continental Crag is a quiet, wide cliff high on the south side of Eldorado Canyon, above the Peanuts walls. All sixteen routes are trad, ground-up and unbolted, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.11 range with a few easier lines. The climbing centers on cracks, dihedrals and roofs, with some face moves between horizontal bands, so bring a full rack and a few big cams for the wider cracks. The best rock is in the upper section toward the southwest end. The face looks northwest, gets light late, and holds snow and cold well into spring. Expect a long, steep approach and a descent that involves scrambling or a fixed rappel.
